title: Migration & Data Transfer
oneLiner: Get data and workloads into AWS: Snow Family, DataSync, Storage Gateway, DMS, and Transfer Family.
examWeightNote: Migration and data-transfer scenarios are a recurring SAA theme — pick the right tool for the constraint.
objectives: Choose an offline (Snow Family) vs online (DataSync) transfer based on data size and bandwidth.
Use Storage Gateway to bridge on-prem apps to AWS storage.
Migrate databases with DMS, including heterogeneous engines via SCT.
Know Transfer Family for SFTP/FTPS into S3 and the AWS migration strategies (the 7 R's).

services.name: AWS Snow Family
services.purpose: Physical devices (Snowball Edge, Snowmobile) to ship large datasets offline when networks are too slow.

services.name: AWS DataSync
services.purpose: Fast, managed online transfer and ongoing sync from on-prem to S3/EFS/FSx over the network.

services.name: AWS Storage Gateway
services.purpose: Hybrid storage: on-prem apps use local file/volume/tape interfaces backed by AWS storage.

services.name: AWS DMS
services.purpose: Database Migration Service — migrate/replicate databases with minimal downtime; SCT converts between engines.

services.name: AWS Transfer Family
services.purpose: Managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP endpoints that land files directly in S3 or EFS.

keyConcepts: If transferring the data online would take too long for your bandwidth/deadline, ship it offline with the Snow Family (Snowball Edge for TB–PB; Snowmobile for exabyte scale).
DataSync is for online bulk transfer and recurring sync to S3, EFS, or FSx — far faster than scripting your own copies.
Storage Gateway keeps on-prem applications working with familiar NFS/SMB (File), iSCSI (Volume), or VTL (Tape) while data lives in AWS.
DMS keeps the source database usable during migration; for a different target engine, the Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) converts schema/code first.
AWS Transfer Family exposes managed SFTP/FTPS endpoints so partners can drop files straight into S3 without you running servers.
Migration strategies (the 7 R's): Rehost, Replatform, Repurchase, Refactor, Relocate, Retain, Retire.

diagram.caption: Pick the transfer tool by constraint; data lands in AWS storage or databases.
diagram.note: Rule of thumb: too big to send over the wire in time → Snowball; ongoing network sync → DataSync; database → DMS (+ SCT for a different engine).

scenarios.scenario: A company must move 80 TB to S3 within two weeks, but their internet link would take over two months to upload that much data.
scenarios.question: What's the most appropriate transfer method?

options.label: AWS Snowball Edge — ship the data offline on a physical device
DataSync over the existing internet link

scenarios.explanation: When online transfer can't meet the deadline given the bandwidth, the Snow Family moves data offline on a physical device. DataSync is great online but is bottlenecked by the link here.

scenarios.scenario: A team is migrating an on-prem Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime.
scenarios.question: Which combination of services fits?

options.label: AWS DMS for the migration, plus the Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to convert Oracle to PostgreSQL

scenarios.explanation: DMS migrates and can continuously replicate with minimal downtime; for a different engine (Oracle → PostgreSQL), SCT converts the schema and code first.

quiz.question: When should you choose the Snow Family over an online transfer?
options: When you have a tiny amount of data
When the data is too large to transfer over your network within the required time
quiz.answer: When the data is too large to transfer over your network within the required time
quiz.explanation: Snow Family (offline, physical shipping) wins when bandwidth/time make online transfer impractical for large datasets.

quiz.question: AWS DataSync is primarily used for:
options: Fast online bulk transfer and ongoing sync to S3, EFS, or FSx
quiz.answer: Fast online bulk transfer and ongoing sync to S3, EFS, or FSx
quiz.explanation: DataSync accelerates and automates online data movement/sync between on-prem and AWS file/object storage.

quiz.question: AWS Storage Gateway lets on-prem applications:
options: Use local file/volume/tape interfaces backed by AWS storage
quiz.answer: Use local file/volume/tape interfaces backed by AWS storage
quiz.explanation: Storage Gateway (File/Volume/Tape) bridges on-prem apps to AWS storage using familiar protocols.

quiz.question: To migrate a database to a DIFFERENT engine (e.g. Oracle to PostgreSQL), you pair DMS with:
quiz.explanation: SCT converts schema and code between heterogeneous engines; DMS then moves the data.

quiz.question: Which service provides managed SFTP/FTPS endpoints that store files directly in S3?
quiz.explanation: Transfer Family offers fully managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP access that lands files in S3 or EFS without running servers.

quiz.question: In the AWS migration strategies, 'Rehost' means:
options: Rewrite the app to be cloud-native
Lift-and-shift the app to AWS with minimal changes
Replace it with a SaaS product
quiz.answer: Lift-and-shift the app to AWS with minimal changes
quiz.explanation: Rehost = lift-and-shift. The 7 R's also include Replatform, Repurchase, Refactor, Relocate, Retain, and Retire.
